nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a type, let $p$ be a real number with $0 \le p \le 1$, and let $P$ be a property of configurations $\omega$, that is, of functions assigning true or false to every unordered pair $\{a, b\}$ of points of $V \times \mathbb{Z}$ (with $a = b$ allowed). We say that $P$ holds almost surely if $P(\omega)$ holds for almost every $\omega$ with respect to the Bernoulli($p$) bond law on $V \times \mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Almost-sure properties under the Bernoulli bond law

nodes.summary: For a type $V$ and $0 \le p \le 1$, the Bernoulli($p$) bond law on $V \times \mathbb{Z}$ is the product measure on configurations $\omega$, which assign true (open) or false (closed) to every unordered pair $\{a, b\}$ of points of $V \times \mathbb{Z}$ (with $a = b$ allowed), under which the values $\omega(e)$ are independent and each is true with probability $p$ and false with probability $1 - p$.
nodes.title: Bernoulli bond law on $V \times \mathbb{Z}$

The open cluster of $x$ is the set of points $y \in V \times \mathbb{Z}$ that are reachable from $x$ (including $x$ itself) in the open subgraph of $G \times \mathbb{Z}$…
nodes.title: Open cluster in the product graph

The open subgraph of $G \times \mathbb{Z}$ determined by $\omega$ is the simple graph on $V \times \mathbb{Z}$ in which $a$ and $b$ are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in $G \times \mathbb{Z}$ and…
nodes.title: Open subgraph of the product graph

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a countable vertex set $V$, the critical probability $p_c(G)$ is the infimum of the set consisting of $1$ together with every $p \in [0, 1]$ for which, under the Bernoulli($p$) bond law on $V$, the event that the open cluster in $G$ of some vertex is infinite has positive probability. In particular $p_c(G) = 1$ when no such $p$ exists.
nodes.title: Critical probability for bond percolation

nodes.summary: For a type $V$ and $0 \le p \le 1$, the Bernoulli($p$) bond law on $V$ is the product measure on configurations $\omega$, which assign true (open) or false (closed) to every unordered pair $\{a, b\}$ of elements of $V$ (with $a = b$ allowed), under which the values $\omega(e)$ are independent and each is true with probability $p$ and false with probability $1 - p$.
nodes.title: Bernoulli bond law on $V$

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $V$, let $\omega$ assign true or false to every unordered pair of elements of $V$, and let $x \in V$. The open cluster of $x$ is the set of vertices $y \in V$ that are reachable from $x$ (including $x$ itself) in the open subgraph of $G$ determined by $\omega$, that is, joined to $x$ by a path whose edges $e$ are edges of $G$ with $\omega(e)$ true.
nodes.title: Open cluster in a graph

nodes.summary: The integer line is the simple graph on $\mathbb{Z}$ in which $m$ and $n$ are adjacent exactly when $|m - n| = 1$.
nodes.title: The integer line graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $V$ and let $\omega$ assign true or false to every unordered pair of elements of $V$. The open subgraph of $G$ determined by $\omega$ is the simple graph on $V$ in which $a$ and $b$ are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in $G$ and $\omega(\{a, b\})$ is true.
nodes.title: Open subgraph of a graph

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on $V$, the graph $G \times \mathbb{Z}$ is the box product of $G$ with the integer line: its vertex set is $V \times \mathbb{Z}$, and $(v, m)$ and $(w, n)$ are adjacent exactly when either $v$ and $w$ are adjacent in $G$ and $m = n$, or $v = w$ and $|m - n| = 1$.
nodes.title: The product graph $G \times \mathbb{Z}$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
